editorial:
Polina arrives at a new school and quickly becomes a target, but Bars steps in and makes a strange deal: he will protect her if she agrees to be his fake girlfriend and follow his rules. What starts as a survival plan turns into a messy, emotional romance, and you watch two people slowly drop their walls while everyone around them tries to pull them apart. The vibe is dramatic, sweet, and a little dangerous, with plenty of teen tension and moments that make you root for the couple even when they make bad choices.

The acting keeps the story grounded, especially in the quieter scenes where Polina and Bars stop pretending and start being honest. The pacing moves quickly, though some side characters feel too simple and a few conflicts wrap up too neatly. Still, if you enjoy forbidden teen romance with a strong emotional pull, this is easy to recommend. endingExplained: In the final scenes, Bars refuses to keep the fake relationship going and tells the truth in front of the school, risking his reputation to protect Polina. Her family initially pushes them apart, but after seeing how much they care, they soften. The twist is that Bars planned the whole deal to get close to her because he already liked her, not just to control her. They end up together as a real couple, with a hopeful final scene at graduation.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves teen romance with emotional stakes.
